title: Sumsub Alternatives: 7 IDV and KYC Platforms Compared
summary: Seven Sumsub alternatives for KYC, KYB and AML screening, ordered by fit, with honest limits and what to do when the real problem is the review queue.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** The closest Sumsub alternatives for a team that wants KYC, KYB and AML screening from one vendor are Persona, Veriff and iDenfy, followed by Socure, Trulioo, Jumio and Entrust as the fit narrows. The options differ mainly in how much of the review process they include, whether they publish prices, and how far they go beyond verifying people. With identity tied to[42% of the BSA reports FinCEN analyzed for 2021](https://www.fincen.gov/system/files/shared/FTA_Identity_Final508.pdf) , the choice deserves a test on your own traffic, not a feature grid.


Sphinx wrote this list. Sphinx is not an identity verification provider, so it does not appear as a numbered replacement; the seven vendors below are ordered by how closely each one matches Sumsub's combined scope, based on the vendors' own product pages and pricing.


## What Sumsub does well, and why teams still shop around


Sumsub's appeal is consolidation. Its platform spans KYC, KYB, AML transaction monitoring, fraud prevention and Travel Rule, with an operational layer of case management, a workflow builder, a rule engine, FIU reports and an AI copilot. It reports more than 4,000 clients and sells into fintech, iGaming, trading, crypto, mobility and marketplaces. It also publishes prices, which several vendors on this list do not: $1.35 per verification with a $149 monthly minimum on its Basic plan, and $1.85 with a $299 minimum on its Compliance plan, which adds AML screening and address checks.


Teams usually start looking for one of a few practical reasons. Business verification, transaction monitoring and fraud prevention sit on Sumsub's custom plan, so a growing program can outgrow the published price. A bundle is less attractive to a team that already has a monitoring system and only wants verification. Pass rates and document support can also vary in the specific countries a business cares about, and that only shows up in testing.


Stronger controls are a further reason. FinCEN found that[about 1.6 million BSA reports in 2021, covering $212 billion in suspicious activity, related to identity](https://www.fincen.gov/system/files/shared/FTA_Identity_Final508.pdf) , and its[November 2024 deepfake alert](https://www.fincen.gov/sites/default/files/shared/FinCEN-Alert-DeepFakes-Alert508FINAL.pdf) described criminals altering or creating identity documents to get past verification. If you need a primer on the underlying checks, this guide to[identity document verification at onboarding](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/identity-document-verification-for-customer-onboarding) covers them.

## The list, in order of fit


Position reflects closeness to Sumsub's scope for a buyer replacing it outright. A lower position says nothing about product quality. Jumio and Entrust can be the right answer for a team that only needs to verify individuals. Vendor figures below are self-reported unless we say otherwise.


### 1. Persona — Best for building your own flows and review process


Persona is a modular platform for verifying people and businesses, with custom collection flows, workflows for KYC and KYB, link analysis through its Graph product, and sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening. Its Cases product adds configurable review queues, audit logging, SAR templates and Case Review Agents that handle routine cases and surface recommendations on complex ones. That makes it the closest match to Sumsub's operational layer, and it was one of 12 vendors evaluated in[Gartner's July 2026 Magic Quadrant for Identity Verification](https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/8184729) .


Persona suits product and compliance teams that want control over each step. The honest limit follows from that flexibility: someone has to design and maintain the flows. Its entry plan also holds back some services, with the full suite of checks, including KYB, on higher plans.


### 2. Veriff — Best for a self-serve start with published rates


Veriff covers document, face and liveness checks, plus AML screening, proof of address, database verification and business verification with beneficial owners. It reports support for 12,500+ documents across 230+ countries and territories, 50 languages and dialects, and a six-second average decision. Self-serve plans run from $0.80 per verification with a $49 monthly minimum to $1.89 with a $209 minimum, and volumes above 5,000 a month move to custom enterprise pricing.


Veriff suits consumer-facing products and smaller regulated teams that want to start quickly and test before talking to sales. The limit is in the tiers. Trained specialist review and fraud tools begin on the $1.39 Plus plan, so the $0.80 rate is not a like-for-like comparison with a regulated setup. Confirm how AML screening is priced for your plan before you model cost. Veriff appears in the same Gartner evaluation.


### 3. iDenfy — Best for paying only for successful verifications


iDenfy offers identity verification, KYB, and sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening with ongoing monitoring. It reports coverage of 16,000+ documents in 200+ countries and territories and more than 1,000 business customers. Two things set its model apart. It bills per successful verification, so blurry images and rejected fraud attempts do not add to the invoice, and in-house staff check verifications around the clock, with a stated turnaround within three minutes.


iDenfy suits fintech, crypto and gaming teams whose traffic includes many failed attempts, where the billing model changes the math. The limit comes from that hybrid design. A human step means a flagged session can take minutes, not seconds, and customer data passes through a vendor review team, which your privacy and outsourcing reviews should account for.


### 4. Socure — Best for US-heavy programs wanting identity and risk together


Socure pairs identity verification with fraud and risk decisioning on its RiskOS platform, with KYB, watchlist screening and workflow routing available through the same layer. In October 2026 it reported more than 6,000 customers across 190+ countries and said it had acquired Fravity, an agentic operations platform now offered as RiskOS_Agents for investigation work inside RiskOS. Socure appears in the Gartner evaluation as well.


Socure suits banks, issuers and fintechs whose main exposure is identity fraud at account opening, especially in the US, where its published proof points concentrate. Two limits are worth weighing. The value comes from running decisions in RiskOS, which is a larger commitment than swapping a verification API. Its KYB documentation also describes using business data partners, so ask which sources apply in your markets.


### 5. Trulioo — Best for global reach through one API


Trulioo verifies people and businesses through a single API, with KYC data checks, document verification, business verification and watchlist screening. It reports 450+ data sources, 14,000+ document types, 195 countries and 700 million verifiable business entities. It says its routing logic sends each transaction to the best-performing source for that region, which matters in markets where a single database is thin.


Trulioo suits payment, remittance and marketplace companies that need to enter many countries without stitching together regional providers. The limit is that its story centers on data and integration, not on the analyst's screen. Ask how much review tooling comes with it, because a team moving from Sumsub's case management may need to keep or buy that separately. Pricing is by quote.


### 6. Jumio — Best for regulated enterprises verifying individuals


Jumio combines ID and selfie verification, liveness detection, risk signals, AML screening and a cross-customer identity graph that it says holds more than 30 million identities. It reports 5,000+ supported ID types and more than 1 billion transactions processed, and offers workflow orchestration with a single configurable risk score.


Jumio suits large regulated businesses, including gaming and financial services, whose main job is verifying individuals repeatedly over the customer lifecycle. The limit is scope. Business verification is not among the products on the Jumio platform pages we read, so a team with KYB volume should expect to confirm that directly or use a second vendor. Pricing goes through sales, which makes a quick cost comparison harder.


### 7. Entrust — Best for pairing verification with authentication and signing


Entrust completed its acquisition of Onfido in April 2024, and the product now sells as Entrust Identity Verification. It covers document and biometric checks, KYC and AML support, data verification and fraud detection, and it can run alone or extend into authentication, account recovery, digital signing and workforce verification, so the identity established at onboarding carries into later high-risk moments.


Entrust suits enterprises that want identity verification and broader identity security from one supplier. The limit is that much of its distinct value depends on using that wider portfolio, and a team that only wants a Sumsub replacement would be buying less of what makes it different. Business verification is also not among the offerings on its identity verification page, and pricing is by quote.


## When the queue is the real problem


Switching verification vendors can improve pass rates and reduce some manual reviews. It does not remove the work that follows a flagged applicant: pulling registry records, clearing adverse media, checking ownership, comparing a case against your SOPs and writing the note. That work sits behind every tool on this list, and a team whose real complaint is backlog can migrate vendors and find the same queue waiting.


Several vendors now address part of this inside their own products, including Sumsub's AI copilot, Persona's Case Review Agents and Socure's RiskOS_Agents. Those are worth evaluating, particularly when the case stays within that vendor's data.


[Sphinx](https://sphinxhq.com/products/ai-agents) works that queue on top of the verification tool, whichever one you keep. Its AI compliance analysts log into the systems your team already uses, run the KYC, KYB and AML checks across 60+ check types, then prepare the evidence, apply your SOPs and produce a traceable recommendation. Your team retains final approval. Across deployments Sphinx reports a 3.2-minute median case and escalates 3-7% of cases to analysts, and the median time to live is 13 days. Alviere automated 86% of its cases and took handling from 14 minutes to 2.4 minutes per case. Pricing is a platform fee plus usage tiers scoped to your volumes.


Sphinx will not help with a capture or pass-rate problem. It does not collect IDs, run liveness checks or match faces, so you still need a verification vendor. It also matters little if your manual queue is small.


One related gap: verification tools focus on whether an ID belongs to a person, while bank statements and incorporation papers raise a different question, covered in this piece on[document verification versus document fraud detection](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/document-verification-vs-document-fraud-detection) .[Sphinx Doc Fraud](https://sphinxhq.com/products/doc-fraud) checks those files for forgery as one agent in a KYB or KYC workflow, or as a standalone check at $0.45 per document.


## How to choose without a sales call


Start with where your cost and risk actually sit, then work through these questions. Most can be answered from your own data.


- Which Sumsub modules do you use today? List them. Replacing KYC alone is a very different project from replacing KYC, transaction monitoring and Travel Rule together.
- How much of your volume is business customers? The split between[KYC and KYB](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/what-is-the-difference-between-kyc-and-kyb) decides whether person-focused vendors stay on your list.
- Where do your failures happen? Pull pass rates by country and document type, then run the same sample through each finalist.
- What do you pay for a failed attempt? Compare billing rules on your real fail rate, not on the headline price.
- What happens after a flag? Time a manual review from open to close. If that number drives your cost, a new vendor may not change it.
- What can your examiners see? Ask each vendor to show the record of who decided what, and why, for one case.


Keep Gartner's scope in mind if you use its report as a filter. It covered 12 vendors, and Persona, Veriff and Socure are the only three from this list among them, so absence from that evaluation does not settle fit for your program.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Who are Sumsub's main competitors?


Gartner Peer Insights lists Veriff, Jumio and iDenfy among Sumsub's alternatives. Persona, Socure, Trulioo and Entrust (formerly Onfido) sell overlapping KYC and identity verification products. The closest match depends on whether you need KYB, AML screening and case tools from the same vendor.


### Is there a cheaper alternative to Sumsub?


On published entry rates, Veriff starts lower: $0.80 per verification with a $49 monthly minimum, against Sumsub's $1.35 and $149. Those plans include different features, so the fair comparison uses the tier you would actually need. Failed-attempt billing can also move the total, which is why iDenfy's pay-per-success model deserves a calculation on your own fail rate.


### Which Sumsub alternatives also do KYB?


Persona, Veriff, iDenfy, Socure and Trulioo all list business verification on their own pages. Jumio and Entrust do not show it among the products we read, so confirm directly with them. Coverage and ownership depth vary by country, so test the jurisdictions where your business customers are registered.


### How hard is it to migrate away from Sumsub?


The integration is usually the smaller part. The harder work is rebuilding flows and risk rules, deciding what happens to existing verification records under your retention policy, and retraining reviewers on a new case screen. Running the new vendor on a slice of traffic first gives you real pass-rate data before you commit.


### Is Sphinx a Sumsub alternative?


No. Sphinx does not capture documents or verify biometrics, so it cannot replace an identity verification vendor. Sphinx works the manual review queue behind verification, preparing the evidence, applying your SOPs and producing a traceable recommendation, while your team retains final approval.
